title: Double-intercept derivation: printed sign typo
explanation: The original slide prints ya + yx - ba + bx = -yx. Expanding (y-b)(a-x) = -xy instead gives ay - xy - ab + bx = -xy. Cancelling -xy yields ay + bx = ab and therefore x/a + y/b = 1 (when a and b are nonzero). The final intercept equation is correct; the intermediate printed plus sign is a source typo, not a valid algebra step.

title: Signed rho versus geometric distance
explanation: In a signed-rho convention, rho may be negative; the nonnegative perpendicular distance is abs(rho). The sign depends on the chosen oriented normal. Keep the theta range and rho convention consistent: a half-turn theta range pairs with signed rho, while a full-turn range can use nonnegative rho.

title: The sinusoidal plots use normal-form Hough space
explanation: The slides retain a y=mx+b label, but the plotted curves are sinusoids with an angular horizontal axis. A fixed image point gives a straight line b=y-mx in (m,b) space, and a sinusoid rho=x*cos(theta)+y*sin(theta) in (theta,rho) space. The generated wording 'sinusoidal curves using y=mx+b' conflates the stale label with the plot. Preserve the original slide and use this distinction when studying the plots.

title: An unsuitable objective is different from an incorrect optimizer
explanation: The horizontal line illustrates a limitation of minimizing vertical squared residuals for a near-vertical point cloud. Calling it an 'incorrect minimum' is misleading: it can minimize the stated objective while failing to represent the intended geometric line. This is a modeling/parameterization issue.

title: Known-radius intersections estimate the center
explanation: On pages 73–76 the radius is already fixed, so the intersection identifies center parameters (a,b), not an independently estimated radius. Radius becomes an additional unknown parameter in the three-dimensional accumulator on page 77.

title: Complete the line-voting worked example
explanation: Additional teaching: for points (1,2) and (3,4), m=(4-2)/(3-1)=1 and b=2-1*1=1, so y=x+1. In normal form choose theta=135 degrees (3*pi/4): cos(theta)=-1/sqrt(2), sin(theta)=1/sqrt(2). Both points then give rho=(y-x)/sqrt(2)=1/sqrt(2). Their voting curves therefore meet at this line parameter. These numeric inputs are a new teaching example, not values claimed to appear in the lecture.
